purpose: Test whether retaining noncontiguous past memory entries within the existing represented spatial-token budget changes automatic Lean segmentation compared with the already evaluated recent-token window. This is a deterministic distributed-history control, not learned usefulness or token-level optimization.
method: Reuse the identical isolated Lean token-window worktree, indexed RoPE, author compression, insurance reserve, model, prompting and image pipeline. Keep the sole conditioning entry and newest entry in full. On each admission, compress pending entries using the original runtime; if remaining resident and newest entries exceed the 16384 feature-token budget with 3072 reserved for the author insurance bank, repeatedly evict the older entry whose removal joins the smallest time span between adjacent retained entries, with the conditioning frame as left boundary and the newest entry protected. Break exact ties by evicting the more recent candidate. Feature/position entries stay paired and pointers and prediction state are preserved. Decide from currently resident entries only; evicted entries cannot be recovered. Unequal token sizes can leave unused capacity.
scope: First engineering sequence 3, then previously inspected difficult sequences 8,11,20 and inset-excluded 23. The primary comparison is the existing automatic raw-recent token window with the same prompt and nominal budget; report actual spatial/pointer keys and frame IDs to assess whether they match. No native or Lean ground-truth baseline reruns, no later detector search, no new inference threshold or confidence gate, no labels or learned weights used for policy decisions.
verification: Synthetic tests check budgets, whole entries, position/pointer preservation, chronological constraints, deterministic tie rule and noncontiguous retention. Require two independent no-op and two candidate sequence 3 runs, exact no-op, parameter and prompt identity, temporal spread beyond recency, budget and pointer accounting, independently reconstructed eviction decisions, and repeated no-inset crop smoke runs. Freeze predictions and then audit saved masks, present-frame Dice, labeled-empty false alarms, per-frame token counts and age distributions versus recent-window and historical GT-prompt references with appropriate prompt caveats.
limits: This tests spread in retained frame ages, not foreground/background utility or causal benefit of specific tokens. Old temporal ages share the oldest learned embedding, and altered masks feed back into memory. Different content can affect future attention and selection. Only represented feature and insurance tokens are counted, not positional tensors, pointers, masks, other state, transient memory or latency. Previously inspected sequences are exploratory and patient independence is unknown.
